title: Carlo Ancelotti fumes as Atletico are awarded a controversial penalty in the Madrid derby - amid Real's 'outrage over refereeing standards' in LaLiga
text:
Carlo Ancelotti was with the penalty granted to Atlético de Madrid in his tie with Real at Bernabéu on Saturday night.
The shock of the upper part of the table ended at a dead point of 1-1 after goals by Julian Álvarez and Kylian Mbappe on both sides of part time, but he was the true boss who let the detachment of his team ruined and the decision of the officials who demonstrated decisive in the result.
The local team was penalized in the 30th minute after a union between Aurelien Tchouameni and Samuel Lino in the area. The first had stepped on the foot of the Atlético player after both players could not contact a cross.
The incident was lost by César Soto Grade, however, he was told to the official to review the clash in the Pitchsis monitor for VAR, at which time he gave visitors a penalty.
After the game, Ancelotti insisted that he did not want to ‘enter into a controversy’, but they said that football fans have been perplexed by such decisions in LaLiga this season.
‘I don’t want to talk (about the referee). The penalty has been granted by VAR, ‘said the Italian. ‘The referee was very close and saw it well. I saw another penalty in the athletics of Girona … The people of football do not understand this.
Carlo Ancelotti was not happy with the decision to grant a penalty of Atlético de Madrid against
Aurelien Tchouameni was penalized after stepping on Samuel Lino’s foot after both players could not make contact with a cross
Referee César Soto Grade granted the spot Kick after Var advises him to review the incident
‘I don’t want to go into a controversy that is quite large. It was a uniform and competitive party. As I said, we left the game with a draw, but we encourage. The team was good in the second half.
It occurs after Madrid sent a formal complaint letter to the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) last week, with a copy sent to the High Sports Council of Spain.
The club complained to officiate in its defeat 1-0 by Espanyol on Saturday, with the only goal scored by Carlos Romero.
Real Madrid believed that Romero should have been expelled previously in the match for a Tackle about Kylian Mbappe, but VAR officials maintained the referee’s decision at the launch of showing a yellow card.
After the game, Real Madrid TV shared a clip on social networks of incident reactions, which was labeled as a ‘global scandal’.
“The decision made by the referee and the VAR is inexplicable,” added the coach of Real Madrid, Carlo Ancelotti, after the game.
‘The most important thing is to protect the player and it was a clear fault, a really unpleasant Tackle with the risk of injuries. Fortunately, nothing happened, but there was a risk. The VAR is also there for this.
“We believe that the decision not to show a red card is inexplicable.”
Real Madrid launched a complaint against the Royal Spanish Football Federation last week (in the photo: the president of the club, Florentino Pérez)
Jude Bellingham directed a complaint with X classification in a line player during the Real Madrid raffle with Atlético
Real Madrid also complained that Vinicius Jr had a discarded goal in the game.
A four -page letter from the club described the performance of officials as ‘scandalous’.
The club added that the party was the ‘culmination of a completely discredited arbitration system whose decisions against Real Madrid have reached a point that adulteration and manipulation of competition cannot be ignored’.
Real Madrid was absent from a meeting held by the RFEF, which presented representatives of male professional clubs and the referee committee.
The president of LaLiga, Javier Tebas, said that the League is considering legal actions against Real Madrid after the letter.
In a fierce Derby in Madrid, Jude Bellingham was also heard directing a moody diatribe in a line player. The midfielder was stunned by an early decision of the assistant referee and ventilated his frustration with one of the pitchsis microphones in the Bernabéu.
F ***, man! He heard it scream. ‘F *** OFF!’
Despite his dissenting sample, Bellingham escaped from a reserve, but remains to be seen if LaLiga decides to launch a retrospective investigation.
Madid remains a point of distance from his city rivals after the draw, while Barcelona has the opportunity to close the gap to Atletico in second or only two points on Sunday night.
